properties.statement: [BL-151] Severability is claimed as computed, and only the single-node case actually is
properties.value: {"evidence": "*Found 2026-08-01 by a review of what dynograph-foundation v0.12.0 offers that reflow2 does not use, at Anthony's request. The headline number: reflow2 consumes 8 of 17 dynograph-graph exports, 2 of ~35 dynograph-vector functions, and none of dynograph-game \u2014 there is more unused foundation than used. The full option set, including the ideas NOT filed, is recorded as proposed Decisions (dec:idea-*) so the roads not taken stay in the design's memory.* req:modularity-computed says severability is computed rather than asserted, and cut_structure \u2014 the only thing computing it \u2014 reports articulation points: single nodes whose removal splits the network. That answers *\"what is a single point of failure\"*. It does not answer *\"how separable are these two subsystems\"*, which is the question modularity actually turns on. dynograph_graph::max_flow_min_cut (Edmonds-Karp, exact, unused) returns the minimum-capacity set of EDGES whose removal disconnects a source from a target \u2014 read here as *\"which contracts would you have to sever to split A from B, and how many?\"* Edge weights are already coupling weights, so the capacity means something rather than being invented for the occasion. Lands squarely on [dec:mosa-conformance], which is OPEN and whose own text says reflow2 \"already computes most of the criteria\" \u2014 this names one of the ones it does not. TWO OBJECTIONS, both on the record at dec:idea-severability-cut: min-cut needs a SOURCE and a TARGET and nothing in the design says which two subsystems a user wants separated, so either the user names the pair (a new question) or it runs over leiden community pairs (defensible, but the communities are themselves computed rather than declared); and low cut capacity is not automatically good \u2014 subsystems SHOULD be coupled where the design says so, and a detector rewarding separation everywhere would push toward a design nobody wants, which is the over-selectivity trap is_single_point_of_failure already had to be tuned out of. Size M", "origin": "Migrated from docs/backlog.md BL-151 on 2026-08-07 (epoch:backlog-retired). Size estimate carried from the row: M."}
